## Petal area measurement

Petal area was quantified from flatbed scans (Canon CanoScan LiDE 400;
300 dots per inch) of excised petals scanned alongside a metric ruler for
scale reference. To avoid the subjectivity and low throughput of manual
outline tracing, petal boundaries were extracted using two independent,
fully automated segmentation methods implemented in Python (scikit-image
v0.26.0; van der Walt et al. 2014). The first thresholded pixels within a
fixed hue range in HSV color space, calibrated to the orange-to-yellow
coloration of *Eschscholzia californica* petals. The second applied
Otsu's method (Otsu 1979) to an excess-orange chromatic index
(R − [G+B]/2), selecting a threshold adaptively for each image rather
than assuming a fixed color range. Both binary masks were cleaned with
standard morphological operations (removal of small objects and interior
holes, light closing) before connected-component labeling; detected
regions were flagged for visual review if their area exceeded the
physically plausible maximum for a single petal or if their solidity
(region area relative to convex-hull area) fell below 0.85, indicating a
likely incomplete or fragmented mask.

Pixel counts were converted to area (cm²) using each image's embedded
scanner resolution. This calibration was independently cross-checked, for
each image, against the pixel spacing of the ruler's printed millimeter
graduations, detected via autocorrelation of pixel intensity along the
ruler's long axis; the two calibration sources agreed to within 2% for
the majority of images tested, and discrepancies beyond 5% were flagged
for review rather than silently accepted. For a subset of petals with
pre-existing manual measurements (ImageJ; Schneider et al. 2012),
automated area estimates were compared against the hand-measured values
as an accuracy check. All segmentation parameters, software versions, and
quality-control flags were recorded programmatically with each
measurement batch to ensure the pipeline is fully reproducible; analysis
code is archived at [repository/DOI].

### Open items before this goes into the manuscript

1. **`[repository/DOI]`** needs a real destination — *Evolution* requires
   a data/code accessibility statement (e.g. a GitHub repo + a Zenodo or
   Dryad archive with a DOI).
2. **The hand-vs-automated discrepancy is deliberately not mentioned
   here** — as of this draft, the two automated methods agree closely
   with each other (~13-15 cm² mean) but both disagree with the 5
   existing hand-measured values (~31 cm² mean) by a consistent ~2.3x,
   and a ruler-based independent scale check confirmed the automated
   pipeline's calibration is correct. That points toward the original
   hand ImageJ measurements' own scale-setting as the likely source, but
   this is unresolved. Once traced, it belongs in Results (or as a
   calibration note here in Methods if it turns out to be a persistent,
   structural difference between methods rather than a one-off error in
   the 5 hand values).
3. Confirm the "Canon CanoScan LiDE 400, 300 DPI" detail (from
   `data/raw/plant/petal_weight_3.xlsx`, Sheet1 note) applies to every
   scan batch used in the final dataset, not just the batch that note was
   written for.
